text:
sam: Quick question — should our default QKV memory layout be interleaved (Q,K,V contiguous per token) or planar (all Q then K then V)? I ran some microbenchmarks and results differ by GPU/seq-len.
lina: Interleaved helped our fused attention kernel on A100 for short sequences. Fewer loads per token since head dim is contiguous :thumbsup:
devon: FWIW my runs show NHWC style (batch, seq, head, head_dim) where head_dim is contiguous beats NCHW-like for vector loads. Numbers: interleaved NHWC = 1.12ms, planar NHWC = 1.28ms on A100 for seq=128, heads=16.
matt: That matches my intuition. Interleaved reduces gather operations in the fused softmax+matmul path. But interleaved makes KV cache append/evict easier (single memcpy), whereas planar makes batched GEMM/transpose simpler when doing per-head kernels.
perf-bot: perf run 1763456790: a100-40gb, fp16, seq=512, heads=32 -> interleaved: 3.45ms, planar: 3.51ms (noise). v100 (older): interleaved: 4.1ms, planar: 3.7ms (planar wins).
lina: See — hardware matters. A100 has better vector load throughput for contiguous head_dim; V100 benefits from more coalesced banked access when planar used with per-head kernels.
devon: Also consider transpose costs: our compile path currently emits a transpose if input layout != kernel expected. Transpose for long seqs kills perf (~20-30% depending on seq). We should minimize implicit transposes.
carol: Operationally we need a deterministic API surface. Proposal: add enum QKVLayout = {"interleaved", "planar", "packed_heads"} to runtime config and model metadata. Kernels register supported layouts and a fallback chain.
sam: Agreed. Also need to decide on a default. Maybe default to 'interleaved' for hosted (A100/80 prefs) and allow Dedicated/Private to override per-deployment based on hardware profile.
matt: We should also expose head_stride and token_stride fields in the runtime descriptor so kernels can avoid assumptions about contiguity. That keeps kernel selection logic clean: pick kernel if it supports the strides.
devon: Adding a small snippet of the descriptor we discussed:

```json
{
  "shape": [batch, seq, 3, heads, head_dim],
  "layout": "interleaved", // or "planar"
  "strides": [batch_stride, seq_stride, qkv_stride, head_stride, head_dim_stride]
}
```

sam: Nice. We must ensure strides are 64-bit aligned for our CUDA kernels (we assume 128-bit loads when head_dim % 16 == 0). If not aligned, fall back to generic kernels.
lina: Quantized kernels add more constraints: packed int8 QKV often wants interleaved+padding to 32. Need to document padding rules.
perf-bot: perf run 1763456801: int8, seq=256 -> interleaved+padded: 0.95ms, planar+padded: 1.10ms
carol: Action items:
- sam: draft runtime config PR with QKVLayout enum + stride fields
- devon: add kernel capability registration API and test harness for layout permutations
- lina: collect perf matrix across A100/V100/H100 and add to roadmap
- matt: define default mapping of hardware -> preferred layout

sam: I'll open the PR today. One more question: should we try a hybrid layout — planar Q then interleaved KV to optimize encoder cross-attention patterns? Anyone tried hybrid?
devon: I prototyped hybrid: gains in decoder cross-attn where Q is small and KV cached — but it complicates cache indexing and increases code paths. Complexity cost + maintenance matters.
lina: If we ship layout enum and kernel registry, hybrid becomes just another layout option without global complexity. So ok to keep optional.
matt: Final note: add diagnostic traces so when a slower kernel is chosen we can log "layout mismatch -> transpose triggered" in the console. Helps debug perf regressions quickly.
sam: Thanks all. I'll include telemetry hooks in the PR and tag you for reviews @lina @devon @matt. :rocket:
